title: Skill Roulette: Measuring Skill Invocation Rate Across LLM Coding Agents
why: A registered-report audit of how reliably coding-agent harnesses invoke packaged skills versus completing the task without them, and which skill-metadata, competition, and context factors change that decision.
mechanism: Skill invocation-rate experiment: repeat identical trials, vary skill metadata, competing skills, contextual instructions, and task wording, and compare 4 coding-agent harnesses × 2 models (planned 20,400 trials), including a test of whether making a skill available changes an unrequested action.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): registered report (results not yet collected); 9 pre-registered hypotheses, eight on invocation and one on unrequested actions; comparisons pre-specified and evaluated with Boschloo's exact test within each model and harness configuration.

title: GUARD: Stabilizing Recursive Self-Improvement with Regret Guidance
why: Closed-loop grader-free harness evolution: RSI adapts an editable harness of prompts, skills, tool rules, and memory from experience without weight updates, using directional regret, parallel candidate edits, and a Soft-HURT non-regression gate, then deploys one frozen harness at test time.
mechanism: GUARD decomposes each task into pre-execution self-checks, grades trajectories by directional regret, pins mastered rules while prioritizing newly broken behaviors, selects among parallel edits by critic-free group-relative fitness, and promotes an edit only when a Soft-HURT gate finds gains outweigh regressions, scoping specialized fixes to a gated buffer.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): benchmarks on memory, skill evolution, continual task streams, and domain reasoning; GUARD is reported to improve performance without catastrophic forgetting or memory pollution while substantially cutting deployment token usage (full numeric tables not in the listing/abs excerpt).

title: ARISE: Practical Self-Evolving Memory for Accurate and Cost-Efficient Enterprise Agents
why: Self-evolving memory for enterprise agents: failures are attributed and stored as retrievable micro-memory, then consolidated into macro rules that are accepted only if held-out accuracy rises, without updating model weights, tools, or workflow logic; compared with GEPA.
mechanism: ARISE uses the deployment model or a teacher model to attribute failures and propose corrections, keeps them as retrievable micro memory, consolidates them into macro rules, and accepts a rule update only when held-out accuracy rises.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): 14 enterprise-workflow domains from SOP-Bench and τ²-bench with 5 models; ARISE-Teacher (Claude Opus 4.6 attribution) is reported to gain 10.9 pp on SOP-Bench and 5.8 pp on τ²-bench over the baseline, and 4.5 / 1.4 pp over GEPA; ARISE-Self gains 10.0 pp on SOP-Bench; the teacher setting is reported to use 4.0% fewer model calls and 5.2% fewer output tokens at comparable per-task cost (−1.0%).

title: Safe Personal RSI: Evaluating and Repairing Personal-Agent Updates
why: An evaluation-and-repair component for personal-agent prompt-update RSI (model weights and runtime code stay fixed): proposed reusable instructions are tested, failing cases repeated, changes temporarily undone to guide repairs, and updates adopted only if safety and task checks pass.
mechanism: Safe Personal RSI tests proposed versus current instructions on a 29-case executable benchmark (email, calendar, health, marketplace) plus probes for authorization reuse, memory, and tool-output injection; it repeats failures, temporarily undoes changes to guide repairs, and keeps the current instructions if no version passes.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): across three models and two deliberately risky edits, the procedure rejects 20 of 21 update attempts; an admitted GPT-5.6 Luna repair is reported to reduce attack violations from 10.7% to 0% and raise safe task completion from 89.7% to 100%; under stronger attacks, a repair transferred from Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct to Qwen3-14B is reported to cut violations from 69.0% to 17.9% and raise safe completion from 19.5% to 64.4%.

title: SCAFFOLD: Toward Warrant-Preserving Evidence Transport for Reusable LLM-Agent Skills
why: Formalizes Warranted Reuse Claims and Warrant-Preserving Evidence Transport for reusable LLM-agent skills, treating skill-library maintenance as the problem of which historical evidence remains admissible after the target context changes (position and methods paper; no implemented verifier).
mechanism: A Warranted Reuse Claim is a defeasible, claim-specific authorization tied to a versioned skill, target context, evidence, assumptions, and identified defeaters. Warrant-Preserving Evidence Transport distinguishes evidence admissibility from truth of the supported claim and specifies three-valued applicability and asymmetric context-transfer judgments.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): no empirical superiority result or implemented verifier; the paper states a conditional preservation result and its limits, and outlines a falsifiable longitudinal evaluation comparing WRC-guided policies with version-aware baselines at matched coverage, utility, and review cost.

title: Space-X: Self-Evolving Spatial Agents Weaving Clues into Evidence Chains
why: Self-evolving spatial agents whose Control Agent diagnoses evidence-chain breaks from execution traces and jointly revises tools, interfaces, skills, memory organization, and decision rules, co-evolving capability and evidence use.
mechanism: An Execution Agent acquires, associates, and judges evidence per problem using role-specific memory. A Control Agent diagnoses evidence-chain breaks from traces and revises tools, interfaces, skills, memory organization, and decision rules so that evidence needs guide capability development and usable results guide actions.

title: OpenKAGE: Open-Ended Lifelong Learning in the Open World via Knowledge-Sharing Agent-Group Evolution
why: Open-ended lifelong agent-group evolution: agents accumulate and share situated memories plus transferable experience and skills (with applicability conditions) through a continuously evolving shared knowledge graph, and can transfer that knowledge to a newly initialized group on a different backbone.
mechanism: A two-layer knowledge representation (a memory layer for situated memories and an experience layer for transferable experience and skills that retains reuse conditions) plus a knowledge-sharing mechanism that semantically consolidates textual experience into a shared knowledge graph while executable skills are shared verbatim.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): in Minecraft, agent groups are reported to sustain exploration and reach advanced technological milestones; accumulated knowledge transferred to a newly initialized group on a different backbone is reported to improve survival and exploration progress (full numeric tables not in the listing/abs excerpt).

title: RSIBench-Infra: Can Agents Optimize Their Own Training and Inference Infrastructure at Production Scale?
why: Benchmark of whether agents can optimize their own training and inference infrastructure (engine, kernel, and instruction levels) under production-scale workloads, with changes captured as OCI image layers and scored end-to-end under quality constraints.
mechanism: Twenty training and inference tasks spanning model families and modalities, with deployments of up to 32 accelerators on NVIDIA GPUs and Ascend NPUs. Agents start from official-recipe baselines and may modify the software stack; an OCI image-layer submission protocol captures the changes, and independent evaluation measures end-to-end performance under task-specific quality constraints.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): across all task results, 66.2% exceed 1.10× validated speedup; the authors report that current agents can improve production-scale training and inference performance, but that identifying effective strategies and consistently translating local improvements into end-to-end gains remain challenging.

title: BaseRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of a Base Vision-Language Model via Training-Free Harness Internalization
why: Recursive Harness Internalization: the base model first improves its harness, then writes what the harness adds into its own weights through training-free edits (ReGap/ReKey) on its own responses, so harness-level RSI is the starting object and is then internalized.
mechanism: ReGap supervises every transformer block with the high-dimensional activation difference the harness makes at that block and updates the block's weights along this signal in a low-dimensional subspace. ReKey writes the signal by regression into a few key-value neurons of every block, measuring site and strength on the model's own responses; edits written at different sites compose in one checkpoint without refitting.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): on ten visual reasoning benchmarks, BaseRSI is reported to improve a base vision-language model both in distribution and on held-out benchmarks (full numeric tables not in the listing/abs excerpt).

title: Think Offline, Act in Real Time: Self-Improving Visual Game Agents through Code
why: Self-improving visual game agents that write, test, and revise a program between attempts (code as policy), storing what they learn in retained code, compared with a real-time learned controller and with improving that controller's weights on a single game.
mechanism: Between attempts (at most eight one-minute executions per run), a model writes, tests, and revises a program that then acts while the game runs in real time. This code-as-policy loop is compared with a trained 2B controller that uses real-time chunking (model as policy) and with improving that controller's weights on a single game.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): across 170 GameWorld tasks, code as policy reaches 47.80% mean progress versus 30.90% for the trained controller and leads in all five game categories; improving the controller's weights on a single game is reported to yield only modest gains.

title: Agentic Harness Engineering Beta: Requirement-Centered Evolution of Agent Harnesses
why: Requirement-centered evolution of agent harnesses: simulated users raise issues over multi-turn use, a team implements generalizable changes, and a change is merged only when it resolves a verified requirement and passes review; compared with Meta-Harness and AHE.
mechanism: A three-step loop: (1) user-driven evaluation, in which simulated users raise requirements as issues while working with the harness over multiple turns; (2) team-based modification that implements those requirements as generalizable changes rather than task-specific patches; (3) requirement-driven selection that merges a change only when it resolves a verified requirement and passes review.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): on held-out tasks, pass@1 rises from 21.9% to 33.3% while using 40.8% fewer tokens than Base Harness, and pass@1 is reported higher than Claude Code, Meta-Harness, and AHE; in a blind human A/B test, real users prefer AHE-Beta in 31 of 48 valid pairs and rate it higher on all five dimensions; without further evolution, the authors report pass@1 gains of 15.8 pp (GLM-5.3) and 5.3 pp (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash) over Base Harness.
